clue.text: Luvvie's association a sort of natural justice?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the British actors' trade union, and luvvie is mocking slang for an actor
second meaning: fairness, the body of law based on natural justice

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an actors' union amounts to a kind of fairness.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the actors' union and also the principle of fairness that tempers strict law.

clue.text: Brenda's after a shot, so bung!

definitions.note: bung is British slang for a bribe

indicators.note: after places the queen's letters behind the shot

parts.note: a backhand is a tennis shot
Brenda is Private Eye's name for the Queen, ER, with 's read as is

explanation.surface: The Queen is chasing a tennis shot, and so - throw it!
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts ER behind BACKHAND. 'bung' looks like a verb (throw); it is British slang for a bribe, as is backhander.
explanation.definitionFit: A backhander is a secret payment slipped to someone, the same thing as a bung.

clue.text: Bastard leader on the buzzer backing up a broadcaster

indicators.note: backing up puts the leading letter behind the buzzing insect, at the back

parts.note: a bee buzzes

indicators.note: leader picks only the first letter of Bastard

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: A rogue at the head of an alarm system, reversing a TV company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes B from Bastard and 'backing up' puts it at the back of BEE. The Beeb is the British nickname for the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beeb is the affectionate nickname of the BBC, Britain's public broadcasting corporation.

clue.text: City centre abandoned by Conservative cuts made by yours truly

definitions.note: the setter, Cyclops, is talking about himself

indicators.note: with its centre abandoned, City keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: the word city itself, of which only the outer letters CY survive
lops means cuts off

explanation.surface: The setter boasting of the Tory spending cuts that have emptied a city centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre abandoned' strips IT from City to leave CY. 'yours truly' means the speaker, here the puzzle's own setter, Cyclops.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclops signs this crossword, so the name is what the setter calls himself.

clue.text: Crooked dealer's familiar cut

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., the familiar form of the first name of ... Leeson, the rogue trader who broke Barings Bank in 1995

explanation.surface: A dishonest trader's mate takes his share.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Leeson was the rogue City trader of the mid-1990s; 'familiar' asks for his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick is both the trader's first name and a small notch or cut.

clue.text: Mixing with Left and Right, Edwina's a deposed impostor

indicators.note: mixing the letters together means they are rearranged
deposed means the a is put out of Edwina's

parts.note: taken as written, with the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Edwina Currie, the Tory MP, mingling with both wings of politics and exposed as a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposed' removes A from EDWINAS to leave EDWINS; 'Mixing' rearranges those with L and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler cheats people by deception, the trade of an impostor.

clue.text: Regular viewers of one of our contributors?

definitions.text: Regular viewers of one of our contributors?

parts.words: Regular viewers of one of our contributors?
parts.note: regular can mean square in shape and viewers can mean eyes, so the phrase describes the boxy eyes jokingly given to a heavy television watcher, perhaps the magazine's own TV reviewer

explanation.walkthrough: Square means regular (as in a regular shape) and eyes are viewers; the British jibe is that someone who watches too much TV gets square eyes, like the screen.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes the eyes of a television addict, so they are the organs of a regular viewer.

clue.text: Clare has inclination to put a candidate in the running

definitions.text: put a candidate in the running

parts.note: Clare Short was a Labour MP
a list is a lean or tilt, as of a ship

explanation.surface: The Labour MP Clare Short is inclined to back someone for selection.
explanation.definitionFit: To shortlist someone is to include them on the final list of contenders for a post.

clue.text: Engaged in fellatio — wanton state

indicators.note: the answer is held engaged inside the run of letters across these two clue words

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of fellatio and the start of wanton

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style verdict that a sex act makes someone or somewhere wanton.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowa is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Spring version of Eye?

parts.note: a private eye is also a slang word for a detective that doubles as a man's first name, and the 1990s Irish deputy prime minister surnamed Spring bore that first name

explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is the magazine; a private detective is a private eye or a private dick, and the politician Dick Spring supplies the 'Spring version'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick is slang for a detective, the same job a private eye does, and also Mr Spring's forename.

clue.text: Nut accepted good telling-off

parts.note: nuts is slang for testicles, and a bollock is a testicle
in can mean accepted, as in being in with a group

explanation.surface: Someone crazy took a good dressing-down without complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' looks like a madman, but here it is the vulgar sense. A bollocking is coarse British slang for a severe reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a severe scolding from a superior is called a bollocking.

clue.text: Empty Tory bluster from a bullying leader

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only the outside letters of Tory

parts.note: only the first and last letters are kept
to rant is to bluster loudly

explanation.surface: Hollow Conservative noise coming from a domineering leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant is a cruel, oppressive ruler, a leader who bullies those under him.

clue.text: Dithering oily brat — name this politician!

indicators.note: dithering suggests being in a muddle, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Private Eye mocks the Labour leader as an indecisive, slippery spoilt child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dithering' rearranges OILY BRAT plus N.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair was the Labour opposition leader of the mid-1990s.

clue.text: Corporation wants grass to protrude

definitions.note: corporation is old British slang for a large paunch

parts.note: grass and pot are both slang for cannabis
to belly is to swell or bulge outward

explanation.surface: A big company wants its lawn to stick out, a nonsense business demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company; it is the dated jokey British word for a fat stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A potbelly is a protruding paunch, which old slang calls a corporation.

clue.text: Elite circle reckon they're the ones who put Major's lot in power

definitions.text: the ones who put Major's lot in power

parts.note: the elect are a chosen elite
O is circle-shaped
to rate is to reckon or estimate

explanation.surface: A snobbish inner circle believes it got John Major's Conservatives elected.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the body of voters who decide which party governs.

clue.text: Footing the bill for frolic by Duchess initially? Not out of $1000!

parts.note: a frolic is fun

indicators.note: initially says take only the opening letter of Duchess

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken
a batsman who is not out is still in
a grand, G, is a thousand dollars or pounds

explanation.surface: Paying for a Duchess's fling, with a thousand-dollar price tag; a royal scandal (the Duchess of York's antics) in Private Eye terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes D from Duchess. G for a grand (1000) is slang the solver must know.
explanation.definitionFit: Funding something means providing the money for it, which is paying its costs.

clue.text: Copulation with Ireland's leading character and man of virtue, Ian Paisley?

parts.note: a union is a sexual joining

indicators.note: the leading character of Ireland's is its first letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken
ST, saint, is a virtuous man

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of the stern preacher Ian Paisley as a virtuous man mixed up in sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading character' takes I from Ireland's. Ian Paisley led Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party; the question mark marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Paisley campaigned to keep Northern Ireland in the United Kingdom, the defining Unionist cause.

clue.text: To arouse member could kill someone

definitions.note: a descriptive definition: a thing that could kill someone

parts.note: to fire someone up is to arouse them
an arm is a limb or member of the body

explanation.surface: A smutty warning that getting a man's member excited could be fatal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' wants its rude sense; it is just an arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm is a gun, a weapon capable of killing a person.

clue.text: Outdated court prat swallows what's supposedly unimportant

indicators.note: the outer word swallows the inner one, putting it in its middle

parts.note: a prat is a fool, an ass
the saying goes that size isn't important

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned courtroom fool takes in something trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' puts SIZE inside ASS. The assizes were English county courts, abolished in 1971; 'size doesn't matter' is the sexual joke behind the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The assizes were periodic English criminal courts, replaced by the Crown Court, so now obsolete.

clue.text: Gets naked — that's the Princess's habit

parts.note: Di was Princess Diana, so the Princess's is DI'S
a habit is a garment, here robes

explanation.surface: Stripping off is a royal's regular practice, a gossip-column jibe at Princess Diana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' pretends to mean a custom, but it is clothing, as in a nun's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: To disrobe is to take one's clothes off, so disrobes means strips.

clue.text: Exercise for the troops — one mark of Paula?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a military display or drill performed by soldiers
second meaning: an inked mark on the skin; the TV presenter Paula Yates was known for hers

explanation.surface: A drill for soldiers set beside a celebrity's body art.
explanation.walkthrough: Paula is Paula Yates, a 1990s British TV presenter famous for her tattoos.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a military pageant and permanent decoration on the skin.

clue.text: Sitting in for a tory tub-thumper

indicators.note: the answer sits inside these clue words, spanning their letters

parts.note: the answer spans the end of for, the a, and the start of tory

explanation.surface: A substitute standing in for a Conservative ranter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub-thumper is a loud public speaker, and an orator is someone who makes speeches.

clue.text: The time it takes to develop interest — not in Cuba's revolution

definitions.text: The time it takes to develop

parts.note: I is the symbol for interest in finance formulas

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Cuba with its possessive ending ignored, giving CUBA

explanation.surface: How long it takes for interest in Cuba's revolution to grow, or for it not to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' rearranges NOT IN and CUBA into NCUBATION; I comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Incubation is the period an egg or a disease needs before it hatches or shows.

clue.text: Start to remove clothing and seduce someone the old-fashioned way -

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... buttons or fastenings
second meaning: in dated usage to ... a woman was to seduce and ruin her

explanation.surface: Beginning to undress and wooing in a dated manner.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers unfastening clothes and, in old usage, bringing about a woman's ruin by seduction.

clue.text: Complete lack of character, we hear, this pisspoor TV show host

indicators.note: we hear says the answer is a sound-alike

parts.note: no L, meaning none of the letter el at all

explanation.surface: Private Eye mocking a TV presenter as having no personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is a letter, L (spelled el); 'we hear' says 'no el' is said aloud, giving Noel, as in Noel Edmonds, host of Noel's House Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Edmonds was a popular British television presenter in the 1990s, here scorned by the magazine.

clue.text: Back a bum,…

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the back part of something

explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into the next one with an ellipsis; this half holds two meanings of one word. A bum is the British word for the buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the hind part of something and the buttocks.

clue.text: …dog-eared, American journalist

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the crosswords' stock journalist

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a scruffy, worn-out American hack.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-eared book has worn, folded pages, so it is used and second-hand.

clue.text: What Major's lot would dearly love: to stagger on etc, pathetically with no one doing a U-turn

definitions.text: What Major's lot would dearly love

parts.note: to reel is to stagger

indicators.note: done pathetically, the letters of etc lose their order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a U-turn makes the word no face the other way

explanation.surface: John Major's 1990s Conservatives longing to limp on, with nobody switching sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins REEL to ECT, the jumbled ETC; NO turned round gives ON after I. John Major was the Conservative prime minister then, unpopular in the polls.
explanation.definitionFit: A government trailing in the polls longs to be voted back into office at the next poll.
